Amid ongoing recovery, the FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, consistent with its average inflation targeting framework to allow inflation to moderately exceed 2% for a time and anchor expectations. Forward guidance, QE, and administered rates support transmission and accommodative financial conditions.

Financial Stability Report context (May 2021) tempers the outlook: While financial conditions remain easy, key vulnerabilities are elevated. Asset valuations are stretched with compressed risk premia; corporate leverage—especially among lower-rated firms—remains high; pockets of stress persist in commercial real estate; nonbank financial intermediation exhibits liquidity and maturity mismatches (for example, money market and bond funds), and episodes like Archegos highlight hedge fund leverage and opacity. Banks’ capital and liquidity are strong, but structural issues in market plumbing (such as Treasury market resiliency and CCP margin dynamics) warrant continued monitoring. Household balance sheets have improved overall, yet lower-income households remain more vulnerable.

Bottom line: Policy stays cautiously accommodative to support maximum employment and inflation goals, but the FSR’s elevated-vulnerability backdrop argues for vigilance and a modestly less upbeat tone than a purely macro read would suggest.
